Subject: Regional uptime split — follow-up from procurement call

Jordan — thanks again for the call this morning. Procurement at HexaPay is aligned on a standard uptime target for the US region, but we need an exception model for EU because of the planned on-prem gateway and regulatory routing that will add operational complexity.

High level asks:
- Can Redwood commit to a regionally split SLA (different uptime % by region) rather than a single global number?
- If so, how would monthly service credits be calculated across regions (blended or per-region caps)?
- We prefer credits that are applied against the invoice rather than one-off service-level credits issued later.

Attached is our draft requirements and an example traffic split. We'd like Redwood's proposed template by EOD Friday so procurement/legal can review.

Attachments: hexapay_sla_requirements.pdf (PDF, 3 pages)

Thanks,
Nelson Park
Head of Procurement, HexaPay
procurement@hexapay.com
From: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>

Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 3 Jun 2026 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Regional uptime split — follow-up from procurement call

Nelson — appreciate the clear asks and the traffic split doc. We can support a regionally differentiated SLA and propose the following operational framework as a starting point:

• Regional uptime targets (monthly): US: 99.90%; EU: 99.60% (EU lowered to account for on-prem and routing variability).
• Remedy calculation: per-region monthly remedy applied to that region's billed usage, with a blended cap option. By default we calculate credits per-region, then apply to the next invoice for that region's usage.
• Monthly credit caps: credits per region are capped at 100% of that region's monthly Redwood invoice (absolute cap).
• Blended alternative: if you prefer one line item on your invoice, we can compute a weighted blended uptime (traffic-weighted) and apply a single credit up to 50% of the total invoice (negotiable).
• Escrow option: for larger accounts, we can put a small monthly hold (1–2% of monthly bill) into a remedy escrow that auto-applies for breaches — reduces reconciliation friction.
• Maintenance carve-outs: scheduled maintenance windows (with 72h notice) are excluded from uptime; emergency maintenance will be documented and we commit to post-incident remediation timelines.

Example calculation (June): US 10M tokens (80% traffic), EU 2.5M tokens (20% traffic). If EU falls to 99.0% (1% below target) we propose a per-region remedy of X% of EU invoice, capped by the EU cap. If you want, we can attach a spreadsheet with worked examples.

Next steps: I can send a formal proposal PDF and an XLS with examples. Marissa and Ben are copied for finance/legal redlines. If you like the blended approach we can circle back with exact percentages and cap language for the contract.

Jordan Blake

Nelson — looping in a couple of legal/finance points we typically propose when splitting regional SLAs. Forwarding Jordan's note with inline redlines below.

On Wed, Jun 3, 2026 at 11:08 AM Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com> wrote:
> (see message above)

Our suggested contract language changes:
- Cap definition: change the absolute cap to read "not to exceed the lesser of (i) 100% of the monthly billed charges for the affected region and (ii) the aggregate monthly remedy cap per Section 5.3." This preserves a global guardrail.
- Blended credit option: define the weighted uptime window and require HexaPay to opt into blended credits for a given billing period; otherwise default to per-region.
- Escrow mechanics: escrow funds must be reconciled quarterly and may be refunded if no breaches exceed thresholds for two consecutive quarters.
- Measurement: uptime measured at the regional ingress points listed in Schedule A; customer telemetry will be accepted for discrepancy checks but primary measurement remains Redwood's monitoring within agreed retention windows.

Ben — please confirm the standard wording for maintenance notice and emergency carve-outs.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Jordan / Marissa — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear options. HexaPay procurement is comfortable moving forward with a short pilot:
• Phase 1 (30 days): US at 99.90%, EU at 99.60%, per-region credits applied to each region's monthly invoice; monthly cap = 100% of that region's Redwood charges.
• Phase 2 (after 30d review): move to blended weighted uptime for billing unless issues arise.

We accept the escrow mechanics for the pilot with quarterly reconciliation. Please send the PDF and the redline-ready contract. We'll route to our legal for a fast review and execute via DocuSign.
